headline: US stocks closed higher with the Dow hitting a record as investors rotated back into chips and AI amid a quiet macro backdrop ahead of Fed minutes
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record above 53,000, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also ended higher in a strong post–Independence Day session
- Semiconductor and AI-related stocks led the rebound as investors returned to the chip trade after recent volatility
- Broadcom (AVGO) rose after signing extended multi-year ASIC supply agreements with Apple (AAPL) for custom chips through 2031, supporting Nasdaq and sector gains
- AMD (AMD) jumped after Goldman Sachs raised its price target and announced a Turing AI partnership, Applied Materials (AMAT) rose after Goldman Sachs lifted its price target, and Micron (MU) and Intel (INTC) advanced as optimism around AI and chip demand improved
- TeraWulf (WULF) surged on news of a $19 billion AI infrastructure deal with Anthropic
- Criteo (CRTO) spiked after reports of takeover interest from Vista Equity, while AXT Inc. (AXTI) also posted strong gains
- Hertz (HTZ) and several distressed or SPAC-related names were notable losers, with declines exceeding double digits amid elevated short interest and prior steep drops
- Communication Services and Financials outperformed with gains above 2%, while Information Technology, Utilities, and Industrials lagged, reflecting rotation within growth and cyclicals
- Macro catalysts were limited with services PMI still in expansion and no major new economic data or Fed actions, while traders look ahead to Fed minutes on Wednesday, ongoing tech earnings, Samsung results, SK Hynix IPO momentum, and early releases from names such as PepsiCo (PEP)
